plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (22-layer ZnS/MgF2 dual-band filter) based on feedback directives. Four routes explore: (1) bounded quasi-periodic thickness initialization with two-phase optimizer per directive, (2) alternative Ge/Nb2O5 material pair evidenced for methane sensing, (3) reduced 18-layer count to test complexity-performance tradeoff, (4) maximum 24-layer count with new initialization scheme. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_01' per refinement_chain requirement.

routes.title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Bounded Quasi-Periodic Initialization and Two-Phase Optimizer
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness initialization to a bounded quasi-periodic schedule centered at ~1050 nm with [750, 1250] nm bounds, combined with a two-phase optimizer (pair-wise joint optimization followed by decoupled fine-tuning), will preserve local optical phase continuity and reduce destructive interference spikes compared to unconstrained initialization.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack with alternating high/low index materials, initialized near modal thickness from prior successful iteration, optimized in two phases to maintain phase ramp continuity.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating ZnS/MgF2 pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um passbands
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um stopbands
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds [750, 1250] nm ensure depositable ranges
Two-phase optimization reduces sensitivity to deposition errors
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filtering
expected_advantages: Reduced destructive interference spikes compared to round 2
Better phase continuity across layer interfaces
known_risks: May not reach iteration_01's 0.955 score due to tighter bounds
Two-phase optimizer may converge to local minima
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating ZnS/MgF2 thin-film stack on CaF2 substrate under air incidence. Initialize all layer thicknesses to a quasi-periodic schedule centered at 1050 nm with bounds [750, 1250] nm. Implement two-phase optimization: Phase 1 jointly optimizes adjacent layer pairs (d_i, d_{i+1}) for i=1,3,5,...,21 to preserve local optical phase continuity; Phase 2 decouples all 22 layers for fine-grained thickness tuning. Target: maximize mean transmittance in passbands [3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm] and minimize mean transmittance in stopbands [2500-3100 nm, 4450-5000 nm]. Use coherent TMM solver with normal unpolarized illumination. Output thicknesses_nm array, best_target_score, valid_candidates count, and tightest_margin. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating ZnS/MgF2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: replaces unconstrained thickness initialization with bounded quasi-periodic schedule centered on ~1050 nm, adds two-phase optimizer to mitigate destructive interference spikes observed in iteration_05.

routes.title: 22-Layer Ge/Nb2O5 Dual-Band Filter Evidenced for Methane Sensing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Ge/Nb2O5 material pair, evidenced in literature for methane sensor bandpass filters at 3300 nm center wavelength, will achieve comparable or superior dual-band performance to ZnS/MgF2 while maintaining manufacturability within 24-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Alternating high-index Ge and low-index Nb2O5 quarter-wave stack, leveraging evidenced material pair for IR gas sensing applications.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | Ge | Nb2O5 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 22 (11 Ge + 11 Nb2O5).
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um passbands
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um stopbands
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and Nb2O5 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Material pair evidenced for methane sensor at 3300 nm CWL
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
Bandpass filter design for gas sensing applications
expected_advantages: Material pair has demonstrated performance for methane sensing at 3300 nm
Higher index contrast than ZnS/MgF2 may enable steeper spectral edges
Provides material diversity comparison to ZnS/MgF2 baseline
known_risks: Ge absorption may reduce passband transmittance
Nb2O5 IR optical constants may have higher uncertainty than ZnS/MgF2

routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave alternating stack with reduced layer count to test complexity-performance tradeoff within the 24-layer constraint.
